definitions.explanation: Strong mental fortitude and perseverance. The ability to push through difficulties without giving up.
A person's fundamental character or nature, often used in a negative sense to describe an unpleasant disposition.

examples.japanese: {根性|こんじょう}のある{人|ひと}だ。
{根性|こんじょう}で{最後|さいご}まで{走|はし}りきった。
examples.english: I ran all the way to the end through sheer willpower.

examples.japanese: あの{選手|せんしゅ}は{根性|こんじょう}があるから、{簡単|かんたん}にはあきらめない。
examples.english: That athlete has determination, so they won't give up easily.

examples.japanese: {根性|こんじょう}が{悪|わる}い。
あいつは{根性|こんじょう}が{曲|ま}がっている。
examples.english: That guy has a twisted personality.

examples.japanese: {根性|こんじょう}の{腐|くさ}った{人間|にんげん}とは{付|つ}き{合|あ}いたくない。
examples.english: I don't want to associate with people who have a rotten character.

notes: Sense 1 is positive, praising perseverance and fighting spirit. Common collocations: {根性|こんじょう}がある (to have guts), {根性|こんじょう}で{頑張|がんば}る (to persevere through willpower). Sense 2 is negative, describing someone's unpleasant character. Common collocations: {根性|こんじょう}が{悪|わる}い (bad-natured), {根性|こんじょう}が{曲|ま}がっている (twisted nature), {根性|こんじょう}が{腐|くさ}っている (rotten character). The compound {根性論|こんじょうろん} refers to the belief that willpower alone can overcome any challenge.
